answer: Admission by latency topology: an identity joins only after running a relay that peers ping for 24 hours; median round-trip time to any peer must exceed 30 ms. Each epoch, rotating established agents replay the logs, rejecting pairs under 5 ms as proof one box fakes many. At the wharf where new identities dock, applicants buy truly spread infrastructure, not a fee; a lotus of clustered sybils withers, mutual pings returning instantly. The attacker's bill: servers in dozens of regions plus probe traffic at the zenith of each epoch; cloning it N times costs N hosting bills.
